response.consequence: GET requests to the audit-log endpoint with optimized_pagination=true by a superuser or a member with global access return a 500 for any non-empty result. A negative-offset cursor also causes an error.
response.explanation: The audit-log endpoint passes order_by="-datetime" to OptimizedCursorPaginator. Its get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil directly on getattr(item, "datetime"), which is a datetime, so it raises TypeError. DateTimePaginator avoids this by converting the datetime to a float timestamp times a multiplier (paginator.py:233-236). value_from_cursor also returns the raw cursor.value instead of converting it back to a datetime (paginator.py:238-241). The cursor value is therefore a number, not a datetime, when it is used to filter the queryset. build_cursor calls get_item_key on the results, so any non-empty page hits the TypeError. Separately, with enable_advanced_features=True and a negative cursor.offset, queryset[negative:stop] is sliced. Django querysets reject negative indexing with an AssertionError. The user supplies the offset through the cursor.
response.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses numeric key logic on the datetime field, so the optimized audit-log path fails

response.consequence: A crafted cursor such as `?optimized_pagination=true&cursor=0:-5:0` makes the audit log endpoint return a server error. If the queryset were ever sliced differently, for example after being converted to a list, the same input would read outside the normal pagination bounds. The new branch has no valid use and only adds a failure path.
response.explanation: The `Cursor` constructor in src/sentry/utils/cursors.py accepts any integer offset (`int(offset)`), and the offset comes from the client's cursor string. When `?optimized_pagination=true` is set by a superuser or a member with global access, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` runs with `enable_advanced_features=True`. For `cursor.offset < 0` it then evaluates `queryset[cursor.offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django querysets don't support negative indexing, and slicing with a negative start raises `AssertionError('Negative indexing is not supported.')`. Nothing catches it, so the request fails with a 500. The code comment claiming that Django handles negative slicing is wrong. The comment that this is 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' is not a bounds check. The regular branch clamps with `max(0, offset)`, and this branch skips that clamp on purpose. I did not check whether any tests cover negative offsets.
response.title: Negative cursor offset is passed straight into a queryset slice, giving a 500 or an out-of-bounds read

response.consequence: Traces with very deep span chains are flushed as multiple partial segments instead of one. The segment is split and incomplete.
response.explanation: The loop that follows the redirect hash was reduced from `for i = 0, 10000` to `for i = 0, 1000`. The removed comment said deeper trees may not be joined correctly. Now a parent chain deeper than about 1000 stops before reaching the real set root, so `set_span_id` is an intermediate node. The script still writes `hset(span_id -> set_span_id)` and merges into that intermediate set, so the segment is split across several sets. The change also adds `zunionstore` with default SUM aggregation, so a payload present in both sets gets its score doubled. That distorts the end-timestamp ordering that the new `zpopmin` trimming depends on.
response.title: Redirect-chain walk limit cut from 10000 to 1000 with no replacement handling

response.consequence: Requests with a prev cursor whose offset is negative fail with an AssertionError (HTTP 500) in every BasePaginator subclass. Even where the slice does not fail, the extra-row trim is wrong, so rows can be duplicated or dropped.
response.explanation: The change removes the clamp of the start offset to 0 when cursor.is_prev is true. A prev cursor with a negative offset, for example offset -1 as built by prev-cursor logic, now reaches queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django querysets reject negative indexing with "Negative indexing is not supported". The comment claiming the queryset handles boundaries is wrong. The trim check `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` also still uses the raw offset, so with a negative offset it compares against the wrong length.

replacement.original:
# Performance optimization: For high-traffic scenarios, allow negative offsets
        # to enable efficient bidirectional pagination without full dataset scanning
        # This is safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions
        start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset
        stop = start_offset + limit + extra
        results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])
replacement.text:
stop = offset + limit + extra
        results = list(queryset[offset:stop])

response.title: Negative offset no longer clamped for prev cursors; Django slice raises

response.consequence: A superuser or global-access user who sends `optimized_pagination=true` with a negative cursor offset gets a 500 error instead of a page of results. The feature advertised as "negative offset support" never works. Even if a backend did accept a negative slice, it would return rows from the wrong window.
response.explanation:
When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with `start_offset = cursor.offset`, a negative number. Django querysets do not support negative indexing. They raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The comment saying the ORM handles negative slicing is wrong. The audit-log endpoint sets `enable_advanced_features=True` whenever `optimized_pagination=true` and the user is a superuser or has global access. The cursor offset comes from the request's `cursor` parameter, so a client can send an offset such as `0:-5:1` and trigger the exception. The Django assertion is from my knowledge of Django, not from the snapshot. The negative-offset branch has no test or caller in the snapshot that exercises it.

A related risk is in `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get`. `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated for any non-superuser. If `member` is None, this raises AttributeError instead of falling back to the normal paginator. I did not check whether `member` can be None here.
response.title: Negative-offset path slices the queryset with a negative start, which Django rejects

response.consequence: The previously working audit-log endpoint returns a 500 for non-superuser callers without a member, even when they do not use the new parameter. Any org member with global access, not only admins, can opt into the unsafe paginator.
response.explanation: `enable_advanced` is computed on every request, even when `optimized_pagination` is absent. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is typed `RpcOrganizationMember | None = None`. `request.user.is_superuser or` short-circuits for superusers, so they are safe. Any non-superuser caller whose context has no member (for example, a token-authenticated request that passes OrganizationAuditPermission without being a member) hits `None.has_global_access` and gets a 500. Before this change those requests succeeded. The gate also uses `has_global_access`, which is broader than the "administrators" the comment describes.

other_findings.consequence: The opt-in optimized path returns a 500 for normal requests. Crafted negative-offset cursors also produce server errors.
other_findings.explanation: In paginator.py, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on `getattr(item, 'datetime')`. That is a datetime, not a number, so it raises TypeError. DateTimePaginator converts to a timestamp instead. With `?optimized_pagination=true` as superuser, any non-empty result set therefore fails in build_cursor. Separately, with `enable_advanced_features=True` and a negative cursor offset, `queryset[start_offset:stop]` is a negative slice. Django raises an AssertionError for that, and the code comments wrongly claim the ORM handles it.
other_findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is broken for the datetime-ordered audit log and allows negative offsets

member = organization_context.member
        enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or (
            member is not None and member.has_global_access
